title: A paired PC that removed this one reads as not checked yet, forever
body:
## Summary
The Devices constellation reads only `presence`, so a computer that revoked this one (link `removed_there`) or whose key never arrived (`awaiting_key`) is drawn as a plain hairline captioned "Seen ..." / "Not checked yet", indistinguishable from a peer not probed yet.

## Description
ADR 0140 "Link state" (amended 2026-10-25) made `GET /devices` carry `link {state, since, evidence}` on every peer and says a 401 hello makes `presence` null ("neither sleep nor a broken network"); it adds "The Devices constellation can adopt `link` later." The TS mirror `apps/desktop/src/lib/fleet.ts:35` `PeerView` has no `link`, and `apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/constellation.tsx:119` / `:128` map `presence === null` to "none" / "Seen ...". A person cannot tell "the other PC dropped me - pair again" (the only mend) from "not probed yet". Fixed: mirror `link` in `lib/fleet.ts` and let the caption, the line state and the drawer's "Now" fact read `removed_there` / `awaiting_key` / `stale` with a sentence naming the mend.

## Flow
- Revoke this PC on the other computer (one-sided revoke)
- this PC's probe gets 401 -> presence null, link.state removed_there
- the constellation draws the peer as "Not checked yet" / "Seen 2 h ago" with a plain hairline, indefinitely

## Expected impact
Anyone pairing more than one PC: they would see "removed on that side - pair again" instead of a node that never changes. Could break: the phone's null-presence caption, which must stay (link.state `phone`).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a peer the other side removed is told apart from one not probed
Before: 0 of 3 link states with no presence (removed_there, awaiting_key, stale) drawn distinctly (read: constellation.tsx:112-140, lib/fleet.ts:35-54)
After: predicted 3 of 3, each with its own caption and drawer sentence
Method: simulation - three walked cases from link.py derive(); a render test needs lib/fleet.ts, outside this round's write set
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/peer/presence.py:171-181 view() returns {presence, presence_at, vitals, link}
src/athena/peer/link.py:59 states: phone, awaiting_key, online, stale, asleep, unreachable, removed_there
apps/desktop/src/lib/fleet.ts:35-54 PeerView: no `link`
apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/constellation.tsx:119 presenceOf = peer.presence ?? "none"
docs/adr/0140-one-athena-pairs-devices-over-a-private-overlay.md:396 "The Devices constellation can adopt `link` later."
instrument: devices.test.tsx render cases with a peer carrying link.state removed_there / awaiting_key / stale (fixtures + lib/fleet.ts PeerView.link): 0 of 3 distinct today

title: The online link's flow animates stroke-dashoffset forever, off the motion contract
body:
## Summary
`.sky__flow` (every online peer's line) runs `stroke-dashoffset` in an infinite 2.8 s keyframe, and `.done__tick` draws with `stroke-dashoffset`; the overlay allows transform and opacity only, on the `lib/motion.ts` clock and motion tokens.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/mind.css:341-346` `animation: sky-flow 2.8s linear infinite` with `@keyframes sky-flow { to { stroke-dashoffset: -56 } }` (:364-368); `:1098-1108` `done-draw` on `stroke-dashoffset`. A dash offset repaints the SVG every frame for as long as an online peer is drawn and the level is open, and 2.8 s / linear are literals, not motion tokens. Calm stops it (:1110) and reduced motion plays it once, so the fault is cost and contract, not accessibility. Fixed: a flow carried by a transformed or opacity-pulsed mark on token durations; the tick revealed by transform/opacity or left static. mind.css is the whole Mind scene's stylesheet (imported by view.tsx), so it is outside this round's write set.

## Flow
- open Mind > Devices with one online peer
- Performance panel: a paint every frame on the sky layer for the life of the page
- the same with the change: compositor-only frames

## Expected impact
Battery and fans on a laptop that leaves the Devices level open; the flow would read the same. Could break: the perf budgets if the replacement adds a layer per link.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - no per-frame paint while the sky idles with an online peer
Before: 2 animations on non-composited SVG properties (sky-flow, done-draw); a paint every frame while an online peer is drawn (read from the CSS)
After: 0 non-transform/opacity animations; frames compositor-only
Method: simulation - CSS read; a perf trace needs the real window and `pnpm perf:*`, the director's gate
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a mind.css source-guard test (no @keyframes on stroke-dashoffset, durations from tokens) seeded red on today's CSS, plus a perf trace of the Devices level with one online peer

title: A refused join clears the code the person typed, and Ask to join never reads its busy flag
body:
## Summary
The join form empties the code field on the press, before the daemon answers, so a refused join (a mistyped or expired code) shows its sentence under an empty field; `busy.join` is set by the store and read nowhere.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/wizard.tsx:658` `setCode("")` runs in the click handler beside `void model.actions.join(address, code)`; `apps/desktop/src/stores/devices.ts:255-273` `act("join")` marks `busy.join` and puts a refusal in `errors.join`, which the field shows. The same defect was fixed for Rename this round (47cce4c4). Clearing does stop a spent code being sent twice on success, so the fix must keep that: keep the code until `joining` lists the ask or a refusal arrives, and disable Ask to join while `busy.join`.

## Flow
- Join another PC, type the address and a code with one wrong character
- press Ask to join -> the code field empties at once
- the daemon refuses -> its sentence sits under an empty field; retype all six

## Expected impact
Whoever mistypes a code read off another screen. Could break: a successful join leaving the code in the field if the clear-on-success rule is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refused code stays in the field to correct
Before: 1 refusal case of 1 loses the typed code (read: wizard.tsx:655-659)
After: 0 of 1, success still clears
Method: simulation - walked; the instrument is a driven test like the rename one, left for a worker because clear-on-success depends on the joining list's timing
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: a driven devices.test.tsx case: type a code, press Ask to join, re-render with errors.join -> the code still in the field (red today); with joining listing it -> field empty

title: The Undo bar announces a bare count with a trailing separator: "Forgetting 1 ·"
body:
## Summary
The staged-answer bar's live region reads "Forgetting 1 · " / "Keeping 3 · " - a number with no noun and a dangling middle dot, announced as is.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:464-466`: the `role="status"` span holds `${Forgetting|Keeping} ${figure(n)} · `; the Undo button and the seconds sit outside it (by design, so the seconds are not re-announced). What is kept or forgotten is never named: one contradiction's keep keeps two memories, Keep all keeps n forget offers. Fixed: "Forgetting 1 memory" / "Keeping 3 memories" / "Keeping both" for one contradiction, the separator outside the live region.

## Flow
- press Forget on one offer
- a screen reader says "Forgetting 1 dot"
- sighted: "Forgetting 1 · Undo 6 s left" - 1 what

## Expected impact
Screen-reader users first, everyone second. Could break: sleep.test.tsx pins the exact text ("Keeping 3 · Undo6 s left") and must be strengthened in the same commit.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the live region says what will happen in words
Before: 2 of 2 phrasings carry no noun and end in " · " (sleep.test.tsx pins both)
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - wording one contradiction's keep needs the batch to carry proposal kinds (StagedBatch holds ids only), a store change a worker should weigh
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:464-466 {`${staged.action === "forget" ? "Forgetting" : "Keeping"} ${figure(n)} · `} apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.test.tsx "Keeping 3 · Undo6 s left", "Forgetting 1 · Undo3 s left"
instrument: sleep.test.tsx: the status span's text for forget-1, keep-all-3 and keep-one-contradiction carries a noun and no trailing separator (red today)

title: The RAM bar turns to the warning hue at 85%, a line the gate does not hold work on
body:
## Summary
`vitals.tsx` colours the RAM meter as "past the line where the gate holds work" at 85%, but the gate holds at 92% (`RAM_HOLD_PCT`) and resumes below 85%; 85 is `RAM_ROOM_PCT`, the slot arithmetic's share.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/vitals.tsx:28-30` says "The hold lines the gate uses" and sets `RAM_ROOM_PCT = 85`, used at :190 as `high`; the `Meter` prop doc (:78) says `high` is "Past the line where the gate holds work". `src/athena/vitals/__init__.py:59-63`: `RAM_HOLD_PCT = 92.0`, `RAM_RESUME_PCT = 85.0`, `RAM_ROOM_PCT = 85.0`. Between 85 and 92 on a rising load the bar warns while `held` is null and work runs; the CPU line (90, held only after 3 samples) has the same shape. Fixed: decide what the hue means - "no slot left" (keep 85, fix the words) or "held" (follow the hold) - and say it in one place.

## Flow
- RAM at 88% and rising, nothing held
- the drawer: RAM bar in the warning hue, no held line under the facts
- a person reads a warning the gate does not act on

## Expected impact
Anyone reading a computer's drawer under load. Could break: the 'tight computer' test that pins the hue past 85.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the bar's hue and the gate's verdict agree
Before: RAM 85-92% rising: hue says held, gate says not (2 of 2 thresholds in vitals.tsx copy a constant under a name that is not the gate's hold line)
After: 0 of 2
Method: simulation - which meaning the hue should carry is a reading of ADR 0143, not a figure
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: devices.test.tsx: a drawer at RAM 88% with held null and one at 93% held - the hue follows the chosen rule (one case is red today whichever rule is chosen)

title: A refused "Sleep now" keeps its old reason beside the button after she has slept
body:
## Summary
A not-admitted "Sleep now" answer stays under the button until the next press, so after she later sleeps by herself the old refusal ("Waiting for room: RAM is at 93%") sits beside "She last slept 2 min ago."

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/stores/sleep.ts` keeps `answer` until the next `sleepNow`; `apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:282` shows `answer.text` whenever it was not admitted. The admitted half was fixed this round (4dd8927b: the line goes once its cycle is read back); a refusal has no `cycle_id` to key on, so the store must keep the last cycle id current at the answer. Fixed: store it with the answer and hide the refusal once `view.last.id` moves past it.

## Flow
- Sleep now while RAM is high -> refused, reason shown
- she sleeps on her own an hour later
- the section still shows the RAM refusal beside "She last slept just now"

## Expected impact
Whoever pressed Sleep now and keeps the Brain level open. Could break: a refusal vanishing on an unrelated re-read if the key is wrong.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a refusal is shown only while it is current
Before: 1 of 1 refusals outlive the next cycle (read: sleep.tsx:282, stores/sleep.ts sleepNow)
After: 0 of 1
Method: simulation - a store field plus a render case; left for a worker since it changes the store's state shape
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:282 {answer && !answer.admitted ? {answer.text} : null} apps/desktop/src/stores/sleep.ts sleepNow(): answer set, cleared only by the next press
instrument: sleep.test.tsx: a refused answer plus a view whose last cycle is newer than the one current at the answer -> the refusal text absent (red today)

title: The sky's legend names three link styles; the sky draws six
body:
## Summary
The constellation legend explains online, asleep and out of reach, but the sky also draws a pulsing dotted line (a request waiting), a dotted primary line (this PC's own ask) and a plain hairline (not checked yet, and every phone).

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/constellation.tsx:372-378` renders three `li`s; `:191-215` and `apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/mind.css:332-362` style `pending`, `joining` and the default line too. The legend shows only when a peer exists and is `aria-hidden` (the hidden list carries the words), so it is the sighted reader's key. A phone's line is always the plain hairline, unexplained beside a lit one. Fixed: an entry for every style drawn on this sky (only those present), or captions that carry it.

## Flow
- pair a phone and a PC; leave a request waiting
- the sky shows 4 line styles; the legend names 2 of them
- the phone's plain line has no key

## Expected impact
Sighted users of the Devices level. Could break: a crowded legend at narrow width (it hides under 560 px already).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - every line style drawn has a key
Before: 3 of 6 drawn styles keyed
After: 6 of 6 (or every one present)
Method: simulation - counted from the TSX and CSS; judging the crowding needs the real window
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/constellation.tsx:372-378
apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/mind.css:354-362 .sky__link[data-state=pending|joining] apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/constellation.tsx:212-215 linkState: null presence -> "none" (plain line)
instrument: devices.test.tsx: for the typical fixture plus a pending request, every distinct data-state on .sky__link has a legend li (red today: none/pending/joining missing)

title: A sleep proposal reads a per-proposal busy flag the store never sets
body:
## Summary
`Proposal` disables its buttons with "Answering..." when `state.busy[proposal.id]`, but the sleep store only ever marks `busy.run`; staged and committing rows leave the list instead, so the branch is dead.

## Description
`apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:373` `const busy = model.state.busy[proposal.id] ? "Answering…" : undefined`, passed to 4 buttons. `apps/desktop/src/stores/sleep.ts:222` `mark()` is called only at :268 and :276, with "run". Since 838efb74 answers are staged and `openProposals` drops staged and committing rows. The dead read tells a reader that a sending row is drawn disabled. Fixed: remove the read and its `disabledReason={busy}` props.

## Flow
- grep mark( in stores/sleep.ts -> only "run"
- openProposals drops staged and committing ids
- no render path reaches "Answering…" on a proposal

## Expected impact
Maintainers only. Could break: nothing user-visible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one dead branch removed
Before: 1 dead read feeding 4 props (grep: mark( -> "run" x2; busy[proposal.id] read x1)
After: 0
Method: probe - grep of every writer of SleepState.busy; not built: below this round's reward line
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/stores/sleep.ts:222 function mark(key, on); :268 mark("run", true); :276 mark("run", false)
apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:373 const busy = model.state.busy[proposal.id] ? "Answering…" : undefined
instrument: the zero-writer grep (done), then typecheck/lint/test green with the read removed
